blocks.arabic_text: اِلَي الْبِرِّ، وَاِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِيْ اِلَي الْجَنَّةِ، وَاِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَصْدُقُ حَتَّي يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللهِ صِدِّيْقًا، وَاِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِيْ اِلَي الْفُجُوْرِ، وَاِنَّ الْفُجُوْرَ يَهْدِيْ اِلَي النَّارِ، وَاِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَكْذِبُ حَتَّي يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللهِ كَذَّاباً.
blocks.tamil_translation: “Without doubt, truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness takes one to Jannah. A man keeps speaking the truth until, in the end, his name is written with Allah Ta'ala in the list of the Siddiq (the very truthful). Without doubt, lying leads to wickedness. Wickedness takes him to Jahannam. A man keeps telling lies until, in the end, his name is written with Allah Ta'ala in the list of the “Kadhdhab” (one who lies much),” Hazrat Abdullah (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ عَاصِمٍ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: كَفَي بِالْمَرْءِ كَذِباً اَنْ يُحَدِّثَ بِكُلِّ مَا سَمِعَ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه مسلم، باب النهي عن الحديث بكل ما سمع، رقم: ٧
blocks.tamil_translation: “It is enough for a man to be a liar that he tells others everything he hears (without verifying it thoroughly),” Hazrat Hafs ibn Asim (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said.

blocks.text: Explanation:- Telling others everything one hears without verifying it thoroughly is a kind of lying. Because of this, people's trust in him goes away.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ اَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: كَفَي بِالْمَرْئءِ اِثْمًا اَنْ يُحَدِّثَ بِكُلِّ مَا سَمِعَ.
